newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold sees NLG one bln Asia sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ahold sees NLG one bln Asia sales in 1997.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV said on Tuesday it expected to generate a turnover of over one billion guilders in the Asia Pacific region this year and is looking for further expansion there.
"At the end of this year, we will have between 150 and 200 shops in Asia...We think we will outstrip the one billion guilder turnover mark this year," spokesman Hans Gobes said.
However, his colleague Jan Hol said Ahold's activities in this fast-growing region would continue to be loss-making for a few more years.
"We expect to break even by 1999 or 2000," he said.
In 1996 Ahold's turnover in the region amounted to 56 million guilders and generated a loss of 20.6 million guilders.
Heavy investment in the region would bring further start-up losses until the turn of the century, Hol said.
"If we stopped investing (in Asia) at this very moment we would be profitable straight away," Hol said.
Earlier today, Ahold said sales in the Asia Pacific region totalled 274 million guilders in the first quarter of 1997.
Its operations in the region are in China, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia.

Hol said Ahold was currently exploring further opportunities to expand in the Shanghai region, with its 17 million inhabitants, where Ahold is already active through its joint venture with a unit of China Venturetech Investment Corp (CVIC).
"I'm not sure we will finalise anything this year...But it does look good at the moment," he said.
CVIC has 15 stores which will all be remodelled and the joint venture plans to start building new stores in the Shanghai region in the autumn.
